Direct-match candidates for the target trait (aortic stenosis) are present: PGS005252 and PGS005254 explicitly report “Aortic stenosis” with trait_efo=aortic stenosis, and PGS005255/PGS005256 are closely aligned aortic valve function measures but still use incident aortic stenosis as the phenotyping endpoint. Main limitation: the reported discrimination metric is a full-model C-index with multiple clinical covariates (e.g., T2D, HTN, CAD, lipids, BMI, smoking, renal failure), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be isolated from the visible metadata. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS005254 is the other exact aortic stenosis model (PRS-CS; HR=1.64 with CI) but lacks comparable discrimination metrics; PGS005255 and PGS005256 are aortic stenosis–adjacent valve-function traits with the same incident AS phenotyping and moderate HRs (~1.53) but are not pure disease-label endpoints; PGS004911 is not aortic stenosis (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy) and is therefore a weaker direct match than the aortic-stenosis family but is included only because the visible candidate list contains limited remaining options.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including exact EFO matches (PGS001135: “Arthritis (nos)” with trait_efo=arthritis; PGS004477/PGS004547: “M13 (Other arthritis)” with trait_efo=arthritis). However, overall evidence remains limited/weak for a clearly strong recommendation because the PRS-only signal for arthritis is small (low PGS-only AUROC/R2) and the other exact-label arthritis models (PGS004477/PGS004547) report only an OR without PRS-only discrimination metrics, making them hard to compare. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS004547 and PGS004477 are exact arthritis EFO matches but lack comparable performance metrics; PGS000114 (juvenile idiopathic arthritis) is arthritis-spectrum with clearer AUROC/OR reporting but is subtype/age-restricted; PGS004873 (incident rheumatoid arthritis) is arthritis-spectrum with strong reported C-index but is not the generic arthritis endpoint. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All listed candidates are direct matches to asthma (trait_efo=asthma), so a direct-match exists. PGS001344 is preferred because it has strong endpoint fidelity for generic asthma risk (phenotyping_reported: “Asthma diagnosed by doctor”), uses only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and reports comparatively strong discrimination among the visible set (full_model AUROC 0.66621 with accompanying PGS-only metrics: PGS AUROC 0.64568 and PGS R2 0.05973), which is also plausible relative to the provided asthma heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.1515). Runners-up: PGS001782 has similar endpoint alignment and basic covariates with strong reported full-model AUROC (0.659) and PRS-comparable R2 (Nagelkerke R2 covariates regressed out 0.048844), but less complete metric detail than PGS001344. PGS002061 and PGS001849 are asthma scores from a portability-focused UKB study with supportive partial correlation (0.1184 and 0.1135 respectively) but lack clearer PRS-only AUROC/R2 and come from a framework/portability context. PGS002727 is pediatric-asthma-specific (endpoint mismatch vs generic asthma) but has strong effect-size evidence (OR 1.57) and large validation, offset by unknown covariates and pediatric restriction. Overall confidence is moderate because multiple strong direct-match options exist with different endpoint framings (doctor-diagnosed vs generic vs pediatric) and many candidates report only full-model metrics or non-AUROC/R2 summaries, limiting clean cross-model comparability. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the EFO level (atopic eczema) but differ materially in endpoint fidelity and comparability. PGS002755 is best supported for the generic target “atopic eczema” because its phenotyping_reported is a direct, general endpoint (“Incident atopic dermatitis”) rather than a restricted subtype (moderate-to-severe) or a treatment-induced phenotype (paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis), and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,090,702). It also reports a PRS effect size (HR high vs low PRS 1.249, EUR eval), providing some direct PRS signal evidence.

Key limitation preventing DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY: none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²); several reported AUROCs are full-model and not comparable as PRS metrics per the provided domain guidance. Additionally, PGS004587 is essentially tied on endpoint (“Incident atopic dermatitis”) with similar covariates and a slightly weaker HR (1.153), while PGS001773 reports very high full-model AUROC/R² (0.93/0.49) but on a narrower endpoint (moderate-to-severe AD) and with covariates that could drive the full-model metric, making its PRS-only strength unclear. The remaining paradoxical-eczema scores (PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903) have endpoint mismatch for generic eczema risk despite being eczema-related.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (atrial fibrillation) by trait_reported/trait_efo and generally consistent phenotyping_reported. PGS005168 is best supported because it comes from a disease-focused AF meta-analysis publication (“Meta-analysis of genome-wide associations and polygenic risk prediction for atrial fibrillation in more than 180,000 cases.”), reports strong discrimination in the selected European validation record (C-index 0.8718 with CI) with basic covariates including CHARGE-AF (a named clinical risk calculator, which is a comparability concern per domain_knowledge), and has extensive supporting validation metadata (record_count 45) plus a plausible per-SD HR (~1.67). The main limitation preventing High confidence is that the reported C-index is a full-model metric with CHARGE-AF included (risk-wrapper packaging), and no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so the PRS-only contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates.

Runners-up: (1) PGS005313 is also disease-focused and multi-cohort (AFGen/BBJ/FinnGen/MVP/UKB/deCODE etc.), uses PRS-CSx (strong method family), and reports strong AUROC 0.78 with OR 1.82, but lacks PRS-only metrics and has less visible breadth than PGS005168 in this context. (2) PGS002814 is a very large cross-ancestry AF GWAS-based score (Nat Genet 2023) with strong reported AUROC 0.74 and pseudo-R2 0.14 in East Asian evaluation; however, its evaluation ancestry is EAS-only here, reducing general direct-match generalizability if deployment ancestry is unspecified. (3) PGS000016 (Nat Genet 2019) is a classic disease score with LDpred genome-wide construction and reports a PRS-comparable Nagelkerke R2 of 0.029 (below the provided h2_obs ceiling 0.0204 but not directly comparable due to scale/adjustment) plus full-model AUROC 0.77 with basic covariates; it is older and shows weaker PRS-only signal than the newer disease-focused meta-analysis candidates. (4) PGS004290 (Nat Commun 2024) has clean basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), EUR-only evaluation, and a solid AUROC (~0.758) with pseudo-R2 (~0.034), but is a single-study UKB-derived method paper rather than an AF-specific meta-analysis, and still lacks PRS-only metrics. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (all include atrial flutter in trait_efo; one is exact-label atrial flutter). Runner-up ordering: PGS001339 is next-best due to close phenotype alignment (AF+flutter, time-to-event) and similarly reported PRS-only metrics; PGS002050 then PGS001841 are ranked by method/structure and slightly higher partial-r for LDpred2 vs penalized regression, but both remain weaker due to missing PRS-only AUROC/R2 and being from a portability framework.

Direct-match candidates for breast carcinoma are abundant in the provided list (multiple models with trait_efo=breast carcinoma and phenotyping_reported as breast cancer / incident breast cancer). The top runners-up are selected from the same high-support cluster with nearly identical endpoint/covariate structure but slightly lower AUROC/R2: PGS004040 (LDpred2.CV), PGS004025 (LDpred2-auto), PGS004083 (PRS-CS-auto), and PGS004069 (megaprs.CV). All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (either exact cholelithiasis/K80 or a closely aligned composite of cholelithiasis + cholecystitis). All 10 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (kidney cancer) via trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (kidney cancer / renal carcinoma / renal cell carcinoma; several explicitly use incident kidney cancer or malignant neoplasm of kidney). PGS004908 is best supported because it has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Kidney cancer), reports the strongest visible PRS effect size (OR=1.5 per SD, 95% CI 1.43–1.58) and the highest reported discrimination among the pool (AUROC=0.74, EUR evaluation), with covariates that are standard epidemiologic/demographic (age, sex, PCs, BMI, smoking, hypertension) rather than obvious clinical-risk packaging. Main limitation: the AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), so comparability across candidates is imperfect and confidence is reduced. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS000076 and PGS000787 are coherent, endpoint-faithful renal cell carcinoma/kidney cancer models with large EUR validation and similar full-model AUROC (~0.722) plus HR~1.15–1.16; PGS000722 has weaker AUROC (0.567) but still incident kidney cancer with large validation; PGS004690 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (AnnoPred; many variants) but shows only modest AUROC (0.5644) and has unknown covariates, limiting interpretability.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (kidney failure) are present, including PGS000708 (trait_reported/trait_efo: Kidney failure; phenotyping_reported: diabetic kidney failure), PGS004492 and PGS004562 (trait_efo: kidney failure; phenotyping_reported: N18 chronic renal failure). PGS000708 is best supported because it is explicitly kidney-failure-labeled and provides the richest, most interpretable performance evidence in-context (C-index 0.779 plus HR 1.19 with CI) with basic covariates (age time scale, sex, batch, PCs) and large EUR validation (n=135,300). Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS004562 and PGS004492 are exact EFO matches to kidney failure via chronic renal failure (N18) but have unknown covariates and only an OR without CI/AUC/R2, limiting comparability; PGS002237 is not kidney-failure-labeled but is a closely related severe CKD endpoint (stage 3+) from a disease-focused Nat Med study with strong AUROC (~0.78) and OR 1.47, making it a strong near-direct alternative; PGS004158 is a coherent CKD/dialysis endpoint with the best AUROC among the five-biobank CKD family (AUROC ~0.592) but is not kidney-failure-specific and has modest discrimination.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target (knee osteoarthritis) via trait_efo/trait_reported/phenotyping_reported, but the pool has limited PRS-comparable performance reporting (most lack PGS-only AUROC/R²), so the best choice is not unequivocal.

Best pick: PGS002767 is a clean direct endpoint match (phenotyping_reported: “Knee osteoarthritis”; trait_efo: “osteoarthritis, knee”), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,052,275 variants), and reports a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.35, 95% CI 1.3–1.4) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical covariates). Runners-up: (1) PGS002729 is also an exact knee OA match with a disease-focused publication and multi-cohort development list; it reports only a full-model AUROC (0.66) with covariates including BMI (mildly non-genetic), but lacks PGS-only metrics, limiting comparability. (2–3) PGS004549 and PGS004479 are exact knee OA/gonarthrosis matches with genome-wide variant counts and report moderate ORs (~1.37 and ~1.32), but have “Unknown” covariates, reducing interpretability. (4) PGS001192 has explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.5566; PGS R² 0.0068) and incremental AUROC (0.0104), but it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”) and uses a time-to-event endpoint, both of which are negative signals versus disease-focused alternatives.

Main limitation: no candidate provides a clearly superior, directly comparable PRS-only discrimination metric across the set; therefore selection rests heavily on endpoint fidelity + method structure + effect-size evidence, yielding only moderate confidence.

All 5 visible candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo = late-onset Alzheimer's disease). The strongest PRS-comparable evidence among them is from the Neurology study pair using genome-wide significant variants with basic covariates (age, sex): PGS000054 shows a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93) in an explicit evaluation ancestry (AMR/Hispanic or Latin American), which is stronger than PGS000053’s OR=1.29 (EUR eval). However, none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R², and several have endpoint/metric comparability issues: PGS000334 reports R²=0.191 from a C+T model with unknown covariates (a value that is high relative to the provided local heritability sanity-check context, making it hard to interpret as PRS-only), PGS004918 reports only a full-model AUROC=0.731 with unknown covariates and very small validation (n=136), and PGS002289’s phenotyping_reported appears to be a cognition-by-age interaction outcome rather than a direct LOAD diagnosis endpoint despite the trait label. These limitations prevent a high-confidence ‘best’ choice, but PGS000054 is preferred on the combination of direct endpoint labeling, clean/basic covariates, and strongest reported per-SD OR among the pool.

Direct-match candidates for lung cancer are present (multiple models with trait_reported/phenotyping_reported as lung cancer or closely overlapping lung/bronchus cancer). PGS000078 is best supported on endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: incident lung cancer), large European evaluation (n=392,539; EUR-only GWAS/EVAL), and the strongest/most complete visible performance package among broadly comparable candidates (full-model AUROC 0.846 plus C-index 0.849 and HR 1.16). However, confidence is limited because the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with extensive covariates (including family history, PM2.5, and detailed smoking terms), and no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS000789 is essentially the same lung-cancer incident endpoint and covariate set with identical AUROC/C-index and similar HR (1.17) but uses inverse weights (less directly supported than the original); PGS004860 reports very high AUROC (0.893) and R² (0.49) for incident lung cancer but lacks PRS-only metrics and appears potentially non-comparable/outlier-like relative to the trait heritability ceiling noted in domain knowledge, so it is discounted; PGS000740 has strong disease-focused development/validation scale (n=167,955) and good AUROC (0.811) but targets early-onset lung cancer (<50), a restricted endpoint vs generic lung cancer; PGS000721 is a direct lung cancer endpoint with moderate AUROC (0.738) but smaller validation (n=1,202) and no PRS-only metrics. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are present for lupus erythematosus / systemic lupus erythematosus. PGS002082 is preferred because it is an exact EFO match to the target umbrella trait (“lupus erythematosus”; phenotyping_reported: “Lupus (localized and systemic)”) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (361,553), which is structurally favored for polygenic traits over sparse GWAS-hit scores when PRS-only discrimination metrics are not available. Runners-up: PGS001870 is the same portability-study endpoint match but with a sparser penalized regression and lower partial-r; PGS000328 is disease-focused SLE with relatively high reported full-model AUROC (0.83) but a restricted early-onset phenotype; PGS000754 is a genome-wide lassosum score with large variant count but lower reported full-model AUROC (0.65) and mixed ancestry evaluation; PGS004917 is direct SLE with moderate full-model AUROC (0.696) and reported OR but has unknown covariates and no PRS-only metric.

Direct-match candidates are present for lymphoid leukemia (EFO: lymphoid leukemia) including PGS000788, PGS000077, PGS000645, and PGS002305; several closely related subtype models for chronic lymphocytic leukemia (PGS000646–PGS000651, PGS000874, PGS003453) are also in the visible list. All 7 candidates are direct matches to macular degeneration/age-related macular degeneration by trait fields, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS004606 is best supported overall because it is disease-focused (Nat Genet AMD architecture paper), has a clean direct disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Age-related macular degeneration), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.0M variants), and reports supportive effect-size evidence (OR 1.76 per SD) plus a full-model AUROC (0.71) with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). The main limitation is that it does not report PRS-only AUROC/R², so the AUROC is not directly comparable as standalone PRS performance.

Runners-up: PGS004952 reports a very high AUROC but it appears to be a full-model metric and the AUROC value is inconsistently encoded (84.2 vs 0.842), with small validation size (n=1,232) and a narrower endpoint (late AMD), so it is promising but less reliable from the visible evidence. PGS004607 is a sibling PRS-CS model from the same Nat Genet study family but with weaker reported signals (AUROC 0.65; OR 1.48) and GWAS ancestry AFR with EUR evaluation, making it less supported than PGS004606 for this context. PGS002269 is AMD-labeled but its phenotyping_reported is a retinal layer thickness biomarker rather than direct AMD diagnosis, reducing endpoint fidelity despite multi-cohort context. PGS001013 is an exact-label macular degeneration model but comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("813 traits"), with weak PRS-only AUROC (~0.553) and small PGS-only R² (~0.006), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused alternatives.

Direct-match melanoma PRS candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=melanoma / phenotyping_reported melanoma endpoints). PGS000813 is best supported in the visible list because it has strong endpoint alignment (familial cutaneous melanoma in non-carriers of CDKN2A mutation; still melanoma), reports the strongest discrimination among melanoma-labeled candidates (full_model AUROC=0.77 with CI 0.75–0.79) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR=2.12, 95% CI 1.9–2.35), with European evaluation ancestry. Key limitation: its endpoint is a restricted familial/non-carrier subgroup rather than a general-population melanoma endpoint, and most candidates report only full-model AUROC (not PRS-only metrics), reducing comparability; additionally, some strong general-population candidates exist (e.g., PGS000743 AUROC=0.74 but with heavy traditional risk-factor covariates; PGS002247/PGS002246 AUROC~0.69 for incident invasive melanoma). Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support combining endpoint fidelity and reported performance/effect-size evidence.

All 6 listed candidates are nominal direct matches on concept (trait_reported = Multiple myeloma; trait_efo = plasma cell myeloma), but one (PGS003450) has an explicit endpoint mismatch in phenotyping_reported (Chronic lymphocytic leukemia), so it is deprioritized despite sharing the myeloma label fields. Among the remaining coherent myeloma-endpoint candidates, PGS002281 is best supported by (i) phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported = Multiple myeloma), (ii) comparatively stronger reported discrimination in the visible metrics (full_model AUROC 0.644 with CI 0.622–0.666) and a strong stratification effect (OR highest vs lowest quintiles 3.18, CI 2.34–4.33), and (iii) basic covariate adjustment (age, sex, geographic region) without obvious heavy clinical leakage. Confidence is only Moderate (hence DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL) because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2 are null across the set), making cross-model performance comparisons reliant on full-model AUROC/effect-size summaries that may not be directly comparable; additionally, PGS002306 shows a higher full-model AUROC (0.69) but on a much smaller validation sample (n=290) with unknown covariates, creating unresolved comparability/robustness uncertainty. Runners-up are ranked by remaining endpoint fidelity plus strength/robustness of the visible performance evidence: PGS002306 next (higher AUROC but small n and unknown covariates), then the PRSweb cluster PGS000653/PGS000654/PGS000652 (consistent myeloma phenotyping with basic covariates, but lower AUROC ~0.55–0.58 and weaker effect sizes).

All 7 visible candidates are direct matches to multiple sclerosis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, so a direct-match selection is possible. PGS002726 is preferred because it is disease-focused (IMSGC), endpoint-aligned (multiple sclerosis), EUR GWAS/EVAL aligned, and it reports strong discrimination evidence in the selected European validation record (full-model AUROC=0.80 with an additional large effect-size signal: OR top 10% vs median=15.0). However, confidence is limited because its covariates are listed as Unknown and it does not report PRS-only metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R2), and the validation sample is relatively small (n=938), making the reported AUROC less comparable across candidates. Runners-up: PGS000809 is also disease-focused multi-cohort with basic covariates and reports full-model AUROC=0.765 and R²=0.069; PGS002038 and PGS001831 come from a portability framework paper (penalized regression / LDpred2) with only partial-r reported (no AUROC/R2), but have stronger method/structure than sparse models; PGS001270 has explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC=0.6586; PGS R2=0.029) but is from a pan-trait UKB framework ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation.

Direct-match candidates for myocardial infarction are present (multiple models with trait_efo/phenotyping_reported explicitly myocardial infarction, including PheCode 411.2 MI and acute MI/I21). Among the visible direct MI models, PGS005039 is best supported by (i) tight endpoint alignment (Myocardial infarction; PheCode 411.2; phenotyping_reported: Myocardial infarction), (ii) strong reported discrimination in the selected validation record (C-index 0.7848) and strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.578, 95% CI 1.50–1.67), and (iii) a genome-wide shrinkage method (ldpred) with large variant count (~1.29M) and multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/EUR split), which is supportive for transportability relative to single-ancestry-only evaluations. Runners-up are other near-identical MI PheCode 411.2 models from the same publication family with very similar C-index/OR evidence (PGS005035, PGS005045, PGS005044, PGS005038). The main limitation is that many top candidates are effectively a near-clone set from the same 2024 HGG Adv paper with highly similar endpoints and metrics, making it hard to justify a single clear winner from metadata alone; additionally, several other direct MI candidates exist (e.g., UKB sparse snpnet MI variants and I21 acute MI models) but are either framework-style sparse scores or have less comparable/complete PRS-only evidence in the provided fields, so confidence remains moderate rather than high.

Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS004465, PGS004535), both explicitly aligned to the target via trait_efo="Nasal Cavity Polyp" and phenotyping_reported="J33 (Nasal polyp)", with identical EUR-only development/evaluation context (UKB; DEV/EVAL EUR 100%), same release date/publication family, same variant count, and same validation sample size. However, confidence is limited because covariates are listed as Unknown for both and there are no PRS-only performance metrics (AUC/R2) to corroborate the effect-size difference; additionally, the two models are near-clones from the same study family, making residual uncertainty about comparability and evaluation details hard to resolve from the provided metadata alone.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to nicotine dependence via trait_efo and report the same endpoint label in phenotyping_reported: Tobacco use disorder), so this is a direct-match scenario. Between them, PGS002037 has stronger visible PRS-comparable performance evidence in the selected European validation record (partial correlation 0.0741 [0.0601–0.0881]) versus PGS001830 (partial correlation 0.0557 [0.0416–0.0697]), with broadly similar covariates (basic demographics + PCs), identical training cohort context (UKB portability framework paper), and identical training/validation sample sizes shown. Method/structure also mildly favors PGS002037 (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage; many more variants) over the penalized regression sparse score, but the primary differentiator here is the higher partial-r under the same endpoint family. Confidence is Moderate (not High) because both models come from the same UKB portability framework publication (a known weaker archetype than disease-focused multi-cohort studies) and neither reports AUC/R2 or effect sizes—leaving only partial-r as the comparable metric.

All 7 listed candidates are direct-match on phenotype concept for the target (nodular goiter), with the strongest endpoint-fidelity coming from the three models explicitly targeting benign/nontoxic multinodular goiter (PGS005261/PGS005262/PGS005263 and PGS001814/PGS002022). PGS005262 is best supported because it is explicitly for benign nodular goiter (phenotyping_reported aligns despite minor spelling noise), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with very large variant count (~1.09M), and has the highest reported AUROC among the benign nodular goiter models (full_model_auc 0.5933 vs 0.5876 and 0.5854). Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS005263 (same endpoint/method family/variant scale but slightly lower AUROC), PGS005261 (same endpoint but P+T with far fewer variants and lower AUROC), then the UKB portability-framework scores PGS001814 and PGS002022 (endpoint-aligned to nontoxic multinodular goiter but from a portability framework and only weak partial-correlation metrics ~0.028 and ~0.024). Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because the leading benign nodular goiter models report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates (no PRS-only AUC/R2), making performance comparability and standalone PRS strength uncertain, and two candidates (PGS005273/PGS005274) are case-control contrasts (thyroid carcinoma vs benign nodular goiter) rather than pure nodular goiter risk.

All 10 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (obesity) via trait_efo and/or phenotyping_reported. PGS005235 is best supported on endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported explicitly targets obesity via phecode 278.1), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) with high variant count (709,828), and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.97), which domain guidance treats as strong discrimination evidence when AUC/R2 are absent. Runners-up: PGS004447 is also an obesity ICD10 (E66) score with LDpred2 and very high variant count (1,059,939) but only moderate OR evidence (1.36) and unknown covariates; PGS005154 and PGS005145 are obesity scores evaluated in East Asian cohorts with large variant counts and strong betas but are less generally supported here due to single-ancestry evaluation context; PGS002033 (LDpred2, 846,292 variants) has the strongest PRS-comparable metric among the portability-paper siblings (partial-r=0.0789) but is penalized by framework/portability study archetype and a broad administrative phenotype label. All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but the pool is dominated by framework/benchmarking-style sources and many models lack PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) or have only single effect-size summaries, limiting a clearly high-quality pick.

Best pick: PGS001273 is a clean direct osteoporosis endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Osteoporosis) and is one of the few candidates reporting explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.5685; PGS R² (no covariates)=0.00688) plus incremental AUROC (0.00477) with basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Although its full-model AUROC is high (0.78972), the small incremental AUROC and modest PGS-only R² indicate most discrimination is covariate-driven, consistent with the domain guidance; additionally it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper, which is a known negative signal for external generalization—hence not high-confidence.

Runners-up: (1) PGS001274 is the closest sibling with similarly clean covariates and explicit PRS-only metrics, and slightly stronger PRS-only AUROC/R² and incremental AUROC, but its time-to-event/"without pathological fracture" endpoint is a narrower formulation than generic osteoporosis. Overall limitation: no candidate combines strong endpoint fidelity with clearly reported PRS-only discrimination across robust external validations; many newer models provide only effect sizes or incremental R², and the only explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² models are from a pan-trait sparse framework, keeping confidence at Moderate and the outcome at DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL.

All 11 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (trait_efo = Parkinson disease), but several are actually progression/cognitive-decline endpoints (PGS000056, PGS000211, PGS000777) rather than generic PD risk/status, which weakens them for a generic “parkinson disease” target. Among the models with phenotyping_reported explicitly as Parkinson’s disease, the Lancet Neurology meta-analysis score PGS000903 is best supported in the visible metadata: it is disease-focused, uses a more polygenic construction (C+T with 1,805 variants vs GWAS-hit-only sparse scores), and it reports comparatively strong association evidence (OR top vs bottom quartile 6.25) plus an R² value (0.054) alongside AUROC (0.692), whereas most others lack PRS-comparable metrics. Key limitation: the reported AUROC/R² appear to be from a full model with covariates (PCs, age, sex) rather than clearly PRS-only, and cross-model metric comparability is therefore imperfect; additionally, some competitors have higher full-model AUROC but with heavier covariate packaging (e.g., PGS001774 includes multiple non-genetic risk factors and family history), which is discounted per the provided domain guidance—leaving moderate, not high, confidence. All 4 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level for the target “peripheral vascular disease” (two are explicitly “Peripheral vascular disease, unspecified” and two are “Peripheral artery disease,” which is a closely aligned clinical entity within peripheral vascular disease). The best-supported choice is PGS005217 because it is disease-focused (PAD-specific publication), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (1,296,292), has large multi-ancestry evaluation (n=304,294 across multiple ancestries), and reports a strong PRS effect size (HR=1.66 per SD), which is supportive of meaningful discriminative signal even without PRS-only AUC/R2. Main limitation: its phenotyping is “incident peripheral artery disease” (incident-only) rather than a generic PVD umbrella endpoint, and the only discrimination metric shown is a full-model C-index (0.731) rather than PRS-only metrics, so comparability to other scores is imperfect.

Runners-up: PGS002055 and PGS001843 are exact-label PVD (unspecified) but come from a UKB portability/framework-style paper (“Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”), with only small partial correlations reported (0.0175 and 0.0151 respectively) and no effect sizes; between them, PGS002055 is slightly better on the reported partial-r. PGS005158 is PAD but is a sparse 19-variant GWAS-hits score in a restricted phenotype context (“Peripheral artery disease in type 2 diabetes”) with heavy clinical covariates, and only a modest HR=1.13, making it the weakest direct-match option here.
